item.title: From Learning French to Building My First Mac App
item.description:
Souvoix · Official Website · Mac App Store · Watch Demo

I recently released my first macOS app, Souvoix. The name Souvoix comes from the French words sous and voix, meaning “under” and “voice,” respectively. I wanted the name to reflect what the app does: turning speech into readable, translatable text and generating bilingual subtitles.

It’s designed for people who want to watch foreign-language videos without subtitles. I would say that using LLMs for translation is definitely one of the most cost-effective applications of AI right now. Google’s LLMs are especially good at subtitle translation, and translating an entire video usually costs just a few cents, sometimes even less.

item.title: Automated Transcription and Translation
item.description:
Today, on a whim, I wanted to study various courses in English, like biology and geography. There are quite a few The Great Courses offerings on Bilibili, but based on my previous viewing experience, these courses often use a lot of terminology; just listening—even with English subtitles—I still can’t fully understand them. So I figured I’d add bilingual Chinese–English subtitles to these course videos and then watch them.

The technical plan is straightforward: use yutto to download videos from Bilibili, ffmpeg to extract audio from the videos, whisper.cpp to transcribe the audio into SRT subtitles (by the way, I’m using Apple M3 Silicon), and finally use the DeepSeek API to translate the SRT subtitles.
